branch_provenance.syndrome: Chronic Progressive Multisystem Syndrome with Dermatological and Systemic Features

state.case_summary:
A man in his 80s presented with a 1-year history of purpura, ecchymoses, anorexia, and weight loss. His medical history included alcohol abuse and cognitive impairment. The purpura and ecchymoses, initially periorbital, progressed over the previous 12 months. Elder abuse was excluded.

Examination demonstrated waxy yellow papules and plaques with purpura in the periocular, neck, axillary, trunk, and inguinal regions.

- Laboratory tests: Investigations revealed anemia, abnormal liver function test results, and renal impairment with moderate proteinuria. The patient's serum protein electrophoresis (SPEP) and immunofixation urine protein electrophoresis test results were normal.- Imaging studies: Radiological studies were unremarkable.- Pathology:  4-mm punch biopsy findings:  - Hematoxylin-eosin staining showed upper dermal amorphous eosinophilic deposits  - Congo red staining results were positive  - Polarizing light microscopy demonstrated pale apple-green birefringence  Images:  Figure A - Description: Waxy yellow discoloration of the skin with papules and purpura in the periorbital region  Figure B - Description: Punch biopsy specimen (hematoxylin-eosin, original magnification × 4)  Figure C - Description: Punch biopsy specimen stained with Congo red (original magnification × 10)  Figure D - Description: Punch biopsy specimen under polarized microscopy (original magnification × 10)

excluded_candidates: Competing mechanism: Vasculitis - reason ranked lower due to lack of specific inflammatory markers
Competing mechanism: Hematologic malignancy - reason ranked lower due to normal SPEP and immunofixation results
